integrity.evidence: Exact branching pair-moment derivation and finite-dimensional matrix-algebra proof; standalone rational Taylor checker included.
integrity.literature_priority: qualified; a broader general inverse covariance theorem may exist.

scientific_limitations: Requires known binary branching rate and stationary-root law with a nondegenerate stationary covariance; the canonical formula uses stationarity whitening, without assuming physical isotropic diffusion.
Full time-resolved matrix covariance and exact short-time derivatives are assumed; finite-sample noise and scalar-only readings are not covered.
A third-jet inverse is ill-conditioned near repeated damping eigenvalues; its exact information loss at degeneracy is part of the theorem.
Identifiability is for the model class defined, not for arbitrary OU or unspecified branching processes.
title: Sharp identifiability and a rotation-blindness boundary for clonal Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance
